Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-021.md for WF02-REQ-021 (waitlist placement with computed position display) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-021, commit 152d263. Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's new getWaitlistPosition export, handlers/registration.ts's extended composeRegistrationReply waitlisted branch + one new read call, two new Catalog.registration i18n keys) is real user-visible/behavioral surface -- the actual text a waitlisted user receives changes. Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 3, docs/guides/qa_testing_guide.md, docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-020.md (reference shape), docs/agents/design/REQ-021.md in full, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts (full getWaitlistPosition body, lines 218-272), apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts (full handler + composeRegistrationReply, lines 1-157), the real apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts registration.* catalog block (quoted verbatim), and BACKEND-DEV's already-committed apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts lines 408-533 (its own REQ-021 AC2/AC4 describe blocks) so this spec's cases are independently parameterized, not accidental duplicates.

Each of the 4 acceptance criteria has at least one concrete, judgment-free verification case. Per this project's convention (REQ-019/REQ-020's precedent), none of them merely points at BACKEND-DEV's already-committed tests -- every case below is this spec's own, with its own exact fixture values (different timestamps, different uuids, a different tg_id range 1000000400+, a different target admission value for the flip), and two genuine gaps were found and closed:

1. No existing test dispatches a real Telegram callback through handlers/registration.ts for a waitlisted outcome and checks the actual composed reply string -- registration.db.test.ts calls getWaitlistPosition/registerForEvent directly and only asserts numbers/kinds, never the assembled user-facing text. AC1 and AC4 close this via a real grammy.Bot dispatch harness (reusing REQ-020's established shape).
2. No existing test constructs two waitlisted rows sharing an identical created_at to exercise design section 2.3's id-ascending tie-break rule -- the committed 3-row case uses three timestamps a second apart, never taking the query's tie-break branch. AC2b closes this, run 3x to confirm the outcome does not depend on INSERT/scan order, only on the id comparison itself.

Case-by-case:
- AC1 (capacity fully taken -> response states a position): live dispatch through the real callback handler, checking the admitted reply is unchanged and the waitlisted reply's exact five-line composed string, including a literal 'Your position: 1' line in the correct position between date/time and 'what happens next'.
- AC2 (withdrawing the first of three shifts the second's position 2->1, no write to their row): three sub-cases -- AC2a checks ordering BEFORE the flip for all three rows (not just the delta), flips using 'admitted' (not BACKEND-DEV's 'withdrawn', per design section 0's 'any non-waitlisted value is an equally valid substitute'), and confirms the third row also correctly shifts 3->2 (ruling out a hidden off-by-one that only updates the immediately adjacent row) plus a byte-identical updated_at via .getTime() equality; AC2b is the tie-break case (identical created_at, lower id wins, run 3x for order-independence); AC2c is the defensive null-case (unknown id, and an admitted-not-waitlisted id) with its own fixture, independent of BACKEND-DEV's committed defensive rows.
- AC3 (git grep finds no stored/cached position/rank field): a git grep across non-test .ts files with every match individually accounted for against four allowed categories, plus a schema/drizzle diff-stat confirming zero column/migration changes.
- AC4 (waitlist accepts unbounded registrations, no refusal): live dispatch of 8 past-capacity registrations (BACKEND-DEV's committed test used 6; picked a different sample per this run's own instructions) through the real handler, checking both zero-refusal-text and a correctly incrementing 1..8 position sequence read out of the actual reply strings in tap order.
- AC-catalog (mechanical, added beyond the 4 ACs per this project's REQ-020 precedent): grep-based parity check that both new i18n keys exist in types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts (6/6 expected matches).

Noted ISS-0014's --no-file-parallelism requirement explicitly in the spec's own execution-note section for TEST-RUNNER, and that the live-dispatch harness scripts (AC1, AC4) must not run concurrently with any other DB-backed vitest file against the same scratch Postgres. Also explicitly pointed TEST-RUNNER at REQ-020.md's Shared Setup step 6 for the harness boilerplate rather than re-pasting a second copy of the same script, to avoid the two specs' harnesses drifting apart over time.

Gap found while reading: none that blocks this spec -- BACKEND-DEV's committed registration.db.test.ts correctly covers the core position/flip/defensive/AC4-count properties at the domain-function level; the only gaps are exactly the two closed above (live-handler dispatch, and the tie-break). No design or implementation defect found -- nothing new to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
